ABSTRACT
Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKGs) are a class of structured knowledge representations
that capture the temporal evolution of relationships among entities, and have demonstrated
significant value in applications such as question answering, recommendation systems, and
financial analysis. Compared with traditional static knowledge graphs, TKGs not only re-
quire modeling structural dependencies among entities and relations, but also capturing their
dynamic temporal characteristics, thereby providing essential support for reasoning in dy-
namic environments. However, due to the inherent sparsity and incompleteness of real-world
data, TKGs still contain a large number of unobserved facts and events. Therefore, designing
effective temporal knowledge graph reasoning (TKGR) methods for accurate prediction of
latent knowledge remains a critical research challenge.
With the advancement of deep learning, recent studies have explored integrating multi-
source heterogeneous information in TKGs (e.g., structural information and textual semantics)
with temporal modeling to enhance reasoning capabilities. In particular, language models
have shown strong advantages in semantic understanding and representation, offering a new
paradigm for TKGR. Nevertheless, existing language model-based approaches still face two
key challenges. First, language models rely on sequence modeling, which differs fundamen-
tally from the structured representation of TKGs, making it difficult to effectively capture
complex structural dependencies and global temporal evolution patterns. Second, most ex-
isting methods lack interpretability, as they rely on implicit representation learning without
explicitly modeling the reasoning process, resulting in limited transparency and reliability in
practical applications.
To address these challenges, this thesis conducts a systematic study on temporal knowl-
edge graph reasoning based on structure-enhanced language models. The objective is to de-
velop a unified framework that integrates structural and semantic information through joint
modeling, thereby enhancing the capability of language models to capture complex structural
dependencies and temporal evolution patterns, while improving prediction accuracy and in-
terpretability. The main contributions are summarized as follows:
(1) To address the limitations of pre-trained language models in modeling complex struc-
tural dependencies and global temporal evolution patterns, this work proposes a structure-
enhanced TKGR method based on pre-trained language models. Specifically, the proposed
method integrates graph structural representations with temporal historical information and
explicitly models relational recurrence patterns, enabling the joint modeling of structural in-

formation, semantic information, and temporal dynamics. On the one hand, a time-aware
soft prompt mechanism is introduced to incorporate entity and relation representations from
the graph space into the language model input, aligning structural embeddings with textual
semantics and improving the modeling of high-order structural dependencies. On the other
hand, a global historical recurrence modeling module is designed to capture recurrence phe-
nomena in TKGs by modeling the frequency distribution of historical facts. Furthermore,
time window and time weighting mechanisms are employed to emphasize recent historical
information, thereby enhancing the modeling of temporal evolution. During inference, struc-
tural–semantic modeling and historical recurrence modeling are jointly integrated to achieve
effective multi-source information fusion. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed
method consistently outperforms existing approaches on multiple benchmark datasets, signif-
icantly improving prediction performance and generalization ability.
(2) To address the limitations of existing methods in interpretability, this work further
proposes a structure-aware generative TKGR framework based on large language models.
At the data level, an explainable TKGR benchmark is constructed by extracting query-related
subgraph reasoning chains from real-world TKGs and transforming them into natural language
explanations, enabling unified evaluation of prediction performance and explanation quality.
At the model level, a structure-aware generative reasoning model is developed. Specifically, a
temporal structure-aware encoder is introduced to model historical structural information and
learn representations of entities and relations, capturing structural dependencies and temporal
evolution patterns. A structure –text alignment adapter is further designed to map structural
representations into the semantic space of the language model, enabling effective utilization
of structural information. Finally, through instruction tuning, the TKGR task is reformu-
lated as a generative process, allowing the model to simultaneously produce prediction results
and corresponding reasoning explanations, thereby achieving explicit modeling of the rea-
soning process. Experimental results show that the proposed framework outperforms existing
methods across multiple datasets, achieving improvements in prediction accuracy, explanation
quality, and reasoning consistency, while demonstrating strong robustness and generalization
capability.
In summary, this thesis systematically investigates temporal knowledge graph reason-
ing based on structure-enhanced language models. Starting from structural modeling with
pre-trained language models, the study is further extended to generative reasoning with large
language models. The proposed approaches achieve significant improvements in both pre-
diction accuracy and interpretability, demonstrating the effectiveness of integrating structural
